newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crude prices ease, LLS rebounds late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crude prices ease, LLS rebounds late.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices eased late Tuesday in quiet sideways trading, while Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James grade rebounded off this morning's lows in an apparent correction, traders said.
March West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was trading around $23.80-90 a barrel, flat with late Monday's cash market but down 20 cents from this afternoon's dealings.
The March/April WTI spread held at 48 cents a barrel.
The market shrugged off mixed results from the American Petroleum Institute's (API) weekly U.S. inventory report, which covered the week end Jan 24.
The API results were in line with general expectations. U.S. crude stocks were up 3.73 million barrels, while gasoline was up 1.84 million barrels. Distillate stocks were down 2.85 million barrels.
The grades were erratic, although LLS rebounded from this morning's flat to five cents premium to WTI/Cushing to plus 10 at 15 cents a barrel. Deals were done at five and 10 cents, traders said.
WTI/Midland was last done at WTI/Cushing minus 38 cents a barrel, down three to four cents from trades done earlier in the day.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire last traded at WTI/Cushing minus 50 cents after earlier changing hands at minus 33/38/40 cents a barrel.
West Texas Sour/Midland last traded at minus $1.95 a barrel, down from a $1.82 deal on Monday.
Bonito Sour was heard done at WTI/Cushing minus $1.20/1.25 a barrel.
WTI/Cushing Posting Plus traded at $2.28/2.29/2.30 a barrel.
